questions.explanation: The natural rate of unemployment is the rate of unemployment at which the economy usually sustains due to its structural flaws. It is the rate of unemployment below which the rate of inflation tends to increase and above which the rate of inflation tends to decrease. It neither has to decrease nor has to increase, that is, at this rate the actual rate of inflation and the expected rate are equal. Hence it is an equilibrium rate of unemployment. Where the economy is headed in the long run. In the long run, the Phillips curve at the natural rate of unemployment is perpendicular to the Y-axis. In this situation the entire labor market and the commodity market are in equilibrium.
